recipes.title: German beef goulash, light
recipes.summary: Tender beef brisket, peppers and potatoes simmered in a paprika-rich German goulash. Extra vegetables and less oil keep the shared dinner lighter while the beef stays generous.

steps.instruction: Prepare the beef brisket, potato, onion, bell pepper and garlic in their listed sizes.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef brisket in batches until coloured on several sides.
Cook the onion and bell pepper until softened and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic, paprika and tomato paste until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Add the tomatoes, beef stock, potato and salt and bring the goulash to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer until the brisket and potato are tender and the sauce tastes deeply savoury.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce thickens around the beef and vegetables.
Rest the German beef goulash off the heat before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days and reheat gently until steaming. The goulash freezes well for up to 3 months; thaw overnight before reheating.

recipes.title: German beef goulash
recipes.summary: A deeply savoury German-style beef goulash with tender brisket, potatoes, peppers and onions in a rich paprika and tomato sauce.

steps.instruction: Prepare the beef brisket, potato, onion, bell pepper and garlic in their listed sizes.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef brisket in batches until deeply coloured.
Cook the onion and bell pepper until soft and lightly caramelised.
Stir in the garlic, paprika and tomato paste until fragrant and darkened slightly.
Add the tomatoes, beef stock, potato and salt and bring the goulash to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer until the brisket is tender and the potato has absorbed the paprika sauce.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce becomes rich and spoonable.
Rest the German beef goulash off the heat before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days; the flavour improves overnight. Reheat gently with a splash of beef stock if needed. Freeze for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: German beef goulash, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous pot of German beef goulash with extra brisket and potatoes in a thick paprika-tomato sauce. It is a substantial high-protein dinner for four.

steps.instruction: Prepare the beef brisket, potato, onion, bell pepper and garlic in their listed sizes.
Heat the olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the beef brisket in batches until deeply coloured on all sides.
Cook the onion and bell pepper until soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, paprika and tomato paste until fragrant and slightly caramelised.
Add the tomatoes, beef stock, potato and salt and bring the larger pot to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer until the brisket is very tender and the potato is cooked through.
Uncover and simmer until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Rest the German beef goulash off the heat before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 4 days and reheat slowly until piping hot. Freeze cooled portions for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Aloo chana chaat, light
recipes.summary: A lively Indian snack of chickpeas, tender potato, cucumber and onion tossed with lime, ginger and warm spices. Extra cucumber keeps this vegan version fresh and light.

ingredients.name: potato
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut into small cubes

steps.instruction: Prepare the potato, cucumber, onion, lime, cilantro and ginger in their listed forms.
Simmer the potato until tender but still able to hold its shape.
Cool the potato until it is no longer steaming.
Stir the lime, ginger, cumin, paprika, brown sugar and salt into a sharp, fragrant dressing.
Combine the chickpeas, potato, cucumber and onion with the dressing.
Fold the cilantro through the aloo chana chaat.
Rest the chaat briefly so the flavours settle.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served soon after mixing. Refrigerate for up to 2 days, though the cucumber will soften. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Aloo chana chaat
recipes.summary: Tender potato and chickpeas tossed with cucumber, onion, lime, ginger, cumin and cilantro. This colourful Indian chaat is tangy, savoury and completely vegan.

ingredients.name: potato
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut into small cubes

steps.instruction: Prepare the potato, cucumber, onion, lime, cilantro and ginger in their listed forms.
Simmer the potato until tender but not falling apart.
Cool the potato until warm rather than hot.
Stir the lime, ginger, cumin, paprika, brown sugar and salt into a balanced dressing.
Combine the chickpeas, potato, cucumber and onion with the dressing.
Fold the cilantro through the aloo chana chaat.
Rest the chaat briefly before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 2 days and serve chilled or at room temperature. The cucumber softens over time, so the chaat is best fresh. Do not freeze.

ingredients.name: potato

recipes.title: Italian vegetable frittata, light
recipes.summary: A light Italian frittata packed with spinach, mushrooms and zucchini, finished with basil and a little parmesan. It is a colourful Mediterranean breakfast for four.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Prepare the spinach, mushrooms, zucchini, onion and basil in their listed forms.
Heat the olive oil in a wide ovenproof frying pan.
Cook the onion, mushrooms and zucchini until tender and the mushroom moisture has evaporated.
Fold the spinach into the vegetables until wilted.
Whisk the eggs, whole milk, parmesan cheese, basil and salt until evenly combined.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables.
Cook the frittata on the stovetop until the edges begin to set.
Bake until the centre is just set and the top is lightly golden.
Rest the Italian vegetable frittata before slicing.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and serve cold, at room temperature or gently reheated. Freeze individual slices for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Italian vegetable frittata
recipes.summary: A tender Italian frittata with eggs, spinach, mushrooms, zucchini, basil and parmesan. The softly baked centre makes it an easy Mediterranean breakfast.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Prepare the spinach, mushrooms, zucchini, onion and basil in their listed forms.
Heat the olive oil in a wide ovenproof frying pan.
Cook the onion, mushrooms and zucchini until tender and lightly golden.
Fold the spinach into the vegetables until wilted.
Whisk the eggs, whole milk, parmesan cheese, basil and salt until smooth.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables.
Cook the frittata on the stovetop until the edges begin to set.
Bake until the centre is set but still tender.
Rest the Italian vegetable frittata before slicing.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 3 days. Serve cold or reheat gently so the eggs remain tender. Freeze slices for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Italian vegetable frittata, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous Italian frittata with extra eggs and parmesan, plus plenty of spinach, mushrooms and zucchini. It is a substantial Mediterranean breakfast for four.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Prepare the spinach, mushrooms, zucchini, onion and basil in their listed forms.
Heat the olive oil in a large ovenproof frying pan.
Cook the onion, mushrooms and zucchini until tender and golden at the edges.
Fold the spinach into the vegetables until evenly wilted.
Whisk the eggs, whole milk, parmesan cheese, basil and salt until fully combined.
Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables.
Cook the frittata on the stovetop until the outer edge is visibly set.
Bake until the thick centre is set and lightly puffed.
Rest the Italian vegetable frittata before cutting it into generous slices.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently or serve at room temperature. Freeze individual slices for up to 1 month.

recipes.title: Tamagodon, light
recipes.summary: Soft eggs, mushrooms and onion simmered in a lightly sweet soy broth and spooned over rice. Extra vegetables and less rice keep this vegetarian Japanese lunch light.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Prepare the onion, mushrooms and spring onions in their listed forms.
Stir the vegetable broth, soy sauce, rice wine and brown sugar together.
Heat the sesame oil in a wide frying pan.
Cook the onion and mushrooms until tender and lightly coloured.
Pour in the broth mixture and simmer until the onion absorbs the savoury sauce.
Beat the eggs until the whites and yolks are loosely combined.
Pour the eggs over the vegetables and cook gently until softly set.
Serve the tamagodon over the white rice and finish with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served immediately while the eggs are soft. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat gently until steaming. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Tamagodon

Stir the vegetable broth, soy sauce, rice wine and brown sugar together.

recipes.title: Tamagodon, hearty

Cook the white rice until tender, then keep the larger portion covered so it finishes steaming evenly.

Stir the vegetable broth, soy sauce, rice wine and brown sugar together.

recipes.title: Korean beef bulgogi, light
recipes.summary: Thin beef brisket marinated with soy, rice wine, sesame, garlic and ginger, then grilled with onion. Extra cabbage and less rice keep the Korean dinner lighter.

steps.instruction: Prepare the beef brisket, onion, green cabbage, garlic, ginger and spring onions in their listed forms.
Stir the soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic and ginger into a marinade.
Coat the beef brisket and onion thoroughly with the marinade.
Marinate the brisket in the refrigerator until the savoury seasoning penetrates the thin slices.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan until fragrant.
Heat a grill pan until very hot.
Grill the brisket and onion in batches until caramelised at the edges and cooked through.
Rest the grilled beef briefly so the juices settle.
Serve the bulgogi with the white rice, green cabbage, spring onions and sesame seeds.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate cooked bulgogi for up to 3 days and keep the rice and cabbage separate. Reheat quickly in a hot pan. Freeze the cooked beef for up to 2 months.
